objective: Automatically find a finite future SQL database state which has exactly the same original minimum-sufficient projected state but a different native result. Correctly refine the minimum input projection without invalidating historical finite source scope.

generator.target_selection: All 14 queries in frozen ID order; stop at first independently observed violation.
generator.candidate_moves: For each missing input feature in sorted [t.a,t.b,t.c,u.a,u.b,u.c], for each row in each frozen world, replace exactly one cell with another value from the frozen row_domain.
generator.interpreter: Independently execute original and optimized SQL in unchanged sqlite3; accept only when both agree within each world and source output differs between old/new worlds.
generator.restart_and_reclose: Import unchanged original FLASH V13; require old finite receipt intact, new expanded-world receipt independent, source-bounded future status, selective withdrawal of only new-scope receipt.
generator.costs: Count candidate probes, number of native SQLite calls and elapsed wall time. Strong conventional SQLite search has identical data and is expected to tie.

protected_positive: At least one native counterexample to a world-relative minimal-state projection's unbounded use, and a new basis preserving all original and new worlds.
protected_negative: No automatic promoted universal SQL correctness; retain old 1301-world source certificate; refuse spoofed target SHA/scope; mutation and wrong environment fail closed.
claim_boundaries: Adversarial follow-on is informed by previous run; not independent untouched second source family.
Data-world expansion is not SQL source change or cross-language semantics theorem.
Source-native optimizer is frozen; generator enumerates a predefined one-cell observation grammar, not self-invented grammar.
A strong full-information native oracle may reproduce all findings.
No external repository writes or stakeholder contact.
